title: Interaction scenario compiler and heapline latency reporter
author: Marina Kohler
description:
Motivation: We lacked a compact way to describe multi-turn, multi-tool interaction patterns representative of production traffic and to cheaply compile those patterns into deterministic microbenchmarks. This PR introduces a lightweight scenario compiler that turns a declarative 'interaction garden' DSL into executable workloads, and pairs it with a new "heapline" latency reporter that attributes end-to-end token latency to allocator and kernel-level phases across the stack. The goal is twofold: 1) make it easy to express real-world conversational topologies (branching tool calls, streaming vs batch, variable primer lengths) and reproducibly exercise them in CI and local profiling; 2) produce compact per-bucket 'heapline' traces that correlate allocation hotspots and kernel wait to p50/p95/p99 token latency so engineers can triage perf regressions faster.

What changed: - Added a scenario compiler (tools/scenario_compiler/) that consumes YAML scenario specs and emits deterministic workload runners for both python and go harnesses. The DSL supports stages, branching predicates, stochastic seeds, and KV-cache priming directives. - Implemented an execution backend that replays compiled scenarios with sequence-aware pacing and optional jitter; supports per-request metadata for downstream reporters. - Implemented reporters/heapline/, a compact reporter that samples allocation events and kernel wait windows, aggregates by logical phase (tokenize, model_dispatch, kv_lookup, kernel_exec, postprocess) and emits a small JSON summary and a compact binary trace used for flame reconstruction. - Added a representative interactive suite (benches/interactive_suites/variegated_dialog.yaml) with three production-inspired scenarios: tool-heavy assistant, short-chat bursty, and streaming-longform. - CI integration: a nightly benchmark job that runs the compiled workloads in a mini-cluster (ci/bench-nightly.yml) and publishes heapline artifacts to the perf-bucket. - Tests and docs: unit tests for the compiler, end-to-end runner smoke tests, and docs with examples under docs/bench-scenarios.md.

Checklist: - [x] Scenario DSL design and parser - [x] Deterministic compiler emitting runners - [x] Heapline reporter with phase attribution - [x] Unit + e2e tests - [x] CI job wiring and bucket upload - [x] Docs and usage example

Usage notes: The DSL is intentionally small. Example spec included in benches/interactive_suites/variegated_dialog.yaml. Run with `tools/scenario_compiler/compile.py --input benches/interactive_suites/variegated_dialog.yaml --target python` then run the produced runner under the perf harness. Heapline reports are uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/heapline/YYYYMMDD/<pr>.json and can be visualized with the perf UI importer.

review_comments: Samir: Nice shape. Two asks: a) can we make the DSL deterministic by default (seed override) and b) ensure heapline traces are capped per-run to avoid unbounded uploads?
Marina: Added deterministic seeding; default seed now fixed unless overridden. Added a 'max_trace_samples' option that defaults to 500. Updated docs.
Ava: CI upload looks good but please add ACLs and retention policy to the bucket path. Also can we add a smaller 'quick' scenario for PRs?

Marina: Added a quick/ smoke scenario (benches/interactive_suites/quick_smoke.yaml) and updated ci/bench-nightly.yml to only run full suites on nightly. Bucket upload now sets object lifecycle to 90 days via perf-bucket policy (linked).
Luke: Observed a sporadic flake where kernel exec time dominates at p99 in local runs; reduced timer granularity and excluded noisy syscalls from phase attribution. Re-ran benchmarks: stable.
Mergebot: All CI checks passed; ready to squash-merge.
release_notes:
- Add scenario compiler DSL and deterministic runners for interactive workload generation.
- Introduce heapline latency reporter to attribute token latency to allocator/kernel phases; uploads compact traces to perf bucket.
- Add representative interactive suite (variegated_dialog) and a quick_smoke scenario for PR validation.
- Nightly CI job to run full suites and publish heapline artifacts.
